title: Connect the page to the service
outcome: Show honest request states without losing a customer’s draft.
story: A customer writes a message. The connection drops just after they press Send. The page should keep their words and explain what is known about the request.

frames.explanation: Disable duplicate submission while one request is pending.
A connection failure does not prove the server did nothing. Keep the draft and explain the uncertainty.

sections.title: Give each request a visible state
paragraphs: Represent idle, sending, saved, validation error, sign-in required, and connection failure explicitly. The page should tell a person what happened and what they can do next.

Use the same API contract on both sides. Send JSON, use the correct method and content type, and include the verified session and CSRF token as required. Parse and validate the response before treating it as a created message.

sections.title: Protect the draft
paragraphs: Keep the text while a request is in progress and when it fails. Clear it only after a validated successful response. Disable the Send button while waiting so repeated clicks do not create two simultaneous requests.

A failed network response may happen after the server stored the message. A retry may duplicate it. For important operations, use an idempotency key generated once for the attempted action and reused for a retry; the service should return the same outcome for that key.

sections.title: Connect real processes
paragraphs: Run the frontend and backend from the workspace. The development frontend proxy forwards /api to the local service. For production, the build can be served from the same origin. That avoids guessing cross-origin cookie settings.

The exercise uses prepared HTTP outcomes to teach the UI reducer. It does not make a real request. Your project must use fetch against the running service and inspect the network panel, including denied and invalid requests.

sections.title: Recover deliberately
paragraphs: Show validation errors next to the form. Show a sign-in action for an expired session. Offer a retry after a temporary connection problem, retaining the draft and idempotency key.
Cancel or ignore old responses when a component changes to another record. Test a slow request followed by a navigation. The most recent screen must not be overwritten by an older unrelated response.

words.meaning: A function that calculates the next state from the current state and an event.
A unique action identifier that lets a service recognize a repeated attempt.
The combination of scheme, host, and port used for a web address.

explanation: The spread keeps the existing draft.
Only an acknowledged success clears text.
A connection failure keeps a path to recovery.

exercise.title: A request-state reducer
exercise.brief: Write nextState(state, event). Return exactly draft and status. send enters sending; saved clears draft; invalid, unauthorized, and network preserve it and use invalid, signin, and retry. Ignore send while already sending and ignore unknown events.

steps.title: Begin and finish a request
steps.task: Handle send and saved. Keep text on send; clear it on saved.
steps.hint: Create a new object instead of changing the supplied state.

steps.title: Keep drafts after failure
steps.task: Map invalid to invalid, unauthorized to signin, and network to retry. Preserve draft.
steps.hint: Put the three event/status names in a small mapping.

steps.title: Guard repeated or unknown events
steps.task: When state.status is sending, another send leaves state unchanged. Unknown events also leave it unchanged.
steps.hint: Guard the duplicate before the ordinary send condition.

cases.why: Sending does not discard the draft.

cases.why: The person needs their text to correct it.

cases.why: The outcome may be unknown; keep the draft.

cases.why: The state model rejects a duplicate pending action.

project.title: A connected message form
project.brief: Connect the React form to the real service workspace. Demonstrate each request state using HTTP responses and a stopped service.
deliverables: A frontend using the real API.
Visible loading, success, and failure states.

milestones.title: Make one real request
actions: Start both processes using the README.
Sign in and obtain the CSRF token.
Submit text and retrieve the saved record.

milestones.title: Represent failure
actions: Stop the service and inspect the connection-failure state.

milestones.title: Make retry reliable
actions: Reuse one idempotency key for a retry.
Test that stale responses cannot overwrite a new screen.

acceptance: The form calls the running backend.
Only confirmed success clears the draft.
Duplicate and retry behaviour is documented and tested.
A keyboard user can understand and recover from an error.

tests.expected: Draft remains with a recovery action.
Sign-in is requested without losing text.

project.extension: Add cancellation when switching between orders and reproduce a slow, stale response.
reflection: Which states does the person need to see?
Why can a network error have an unknown outcome?
Where is duplicate protection enforced beyond the button?
